A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOCUS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic ridge-regression experiments in Figure 4 and CIFAR-10 classification experiments in Appendix F, Figure 9.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports additional MIFA comparisons in Figures 4 and 9, with the classification experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: FOCUS and SG-FOCUS retain the same Algorithms 1 and 2, gradient-tracking updates, stored-gradient reuse, and push-pull communication procedures. The added explanations and theorem summary do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic ridge regression under full, uniform, and arbitrary participation, and CIFAR-10 classification under active and passive arbitrary participation with highly heterogeneous data. No dataset or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: MIFA is added as an evaluated comparator in all three regression panels of Figure 4 and both CIFAR-10 panels of Figure 9. Previously evaluated baselines are retained; the new FedVARP and FAST citations do not represent additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated learning rates, local-step counts, client counts, model architecture, heterogeneity parameter, and training budgets are retained. Figure 4 already uses communication cost per model size in v2; Figure 9 continues to report test accuracy against communication rounds.

E4.justification: The existing participation comparisons and data-heterogeneity illustration are retained. No component ablation, sensitivity sweep, additional robustness scenario, or investigation explaining MIFA's divergence is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The retained stochastic-gradient variance assumptions concern theoretical analysis rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds MIFA results showing overlap with FedAvg/FedAU under full participation and divergence under uniform and arbitrary participation. Figure 9 adds MIFA accuracy curves below SG-FOCUS in both participation settings. The existing leading-performance trend for FOCUS/SG-FOCUS is retained.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the FedAvg aggregation index in Eq. (2c) and adds consensus-limit and mass-preservation derivations in Appendix C. New Eq. (33) incorrectly writes p1^T instead of 1p^T, contradicting its accompanying example. The core convergence proofs are retained; main-text Theorem 2 summarizes results already in v2 Appendix E.

C1.justification: The contribution statement narrows linear convergence from 'convex' to 'strongly convex,' matching the retained theorem assumptions. The abstract stops explicitly highlighting the FedAvg limitation analysis, although that analysis remains. The central exact-convergence and novelty claims are retained.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation for the absence of client-number linear speedup in deterministic FOCUS and asserts such speedup for SG-FOCUS. It acknowledges unexplained MIFA divergence and slightly qualifies the applicability discussion for doubly stochastic matrices. The existing Markov-dependent participation limitation is relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: V2 refers only to implementation code in attached supplementary material. V3 additionally supplies an explicit repository pointer beside Algorithm 1 and explains the code's original FedASL name. The reported implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds MIFA, FedVARP, communication-compression work by Huang et al., and FAST references. A new variance-reduction discussion and the MIFA row in Table 1 modestly expand research positioning. Publication updates for existing FedAvg and FedAU references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: V3 adds a conclusion, acknowledgements, a matrix-review appendix, and a main-text stochastic convergence summary and speedup discussion. It relocates the limitations paragraph and edits wording, headings, and author information, while retaining most of the existing narrative and proof structure.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a MIFA row and a communication-cost footnote. Figure 4 is redrawn and relocated, with revised grid and legend styling; Figure 9 gains MIFA traces and legend entries. The remaining figures and notation table are retained apart from layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added MIFA comparisons, explicit code pointer, and corrected strongly-convex contribution statement modestly improve comparative support, reproducibility information, and precision. These gains are limited by the unexplained MIFA divergence and the incorrect consensus formula in new Appendix C, Eq. (33). The central algorithm and convergence proofs remain unchanged.
